counterexample: Let G have vertices {a,b} and edges a→b and b→a. G is cyclic. Any graph on these vertices with the same transitive closure must contain both cross-edges to provide reachability in both directions, so its unique minimum-edge realization is G itself. Thus G has a unique transitive reduction despite being cyclic.
